title: Ops Chorus: SLO Adoption Hackweek Backlog and Role Matrix
content:
Context:
Ops Chorus is a short, cross-functional hackweek (4 working days) with the explicit goal of moving 3 pilot services from metrics-only monitoring to SLO-driven operational readiness. This doc is the event backlog + role matrix + lightweight acceptance criteria. Intended audience: SREs, Platform Eng, Serving Runtime, Product Observability, Solutions Eng.

Why this format?
- Hackweek lowers the barrier: pairing with product owners + engineers produces runnable SLO configs and dashboards versus a long design doc.
- Focused, timeboxed deliverables generate early wins (dashboards, runbooks, canary configs) that help scale the SLO program.

Event objectives (outcomes, not activities)
- Outcome A: 3 services with defined SLOs, working dashboards, and an automated alert-to-incident flow for degraded SLOs.
- Outcome B: One documented rollback/fallback for inference overload (model downgrade + region failover) wired into runbooks.
- Outcome C: A repeatable template (Jira + dashboard + runbook skeleton) that a product team can adopt in < 2 days.

Scope (in-scope for hackweek)
- Pilot services: inference-api-prod, embedder-worker, routing-proxy.
- Deliverables per service: SLO definition file (yaml), dashboard panel, alert rule, short runbook (<= 2 pages), canary rollout plan.
- Non-scope: infra-level fleet provisioning, long-term policy governance (these are follow-ups).

High-level schedule (4 working days)
Day 0 (pre-hackweek prep) - owners pre-reads and dataset collection
- Owners: product + eng should collect 7d metrics slices (latency p50/p95/p99, error_rate, request_volume), present single-pane CSV by EOD.
- Prep ticket: SRV-482 (link above) contains metric queries and raw dashboards.

Day 1 - Kickoff, SLO drafts, quick dashboards
- Morning: 1hr kickoff + alignment (SRE, product, runtime).
- Afternoon: Define SLO candidate (SLO target, window, burn rate rules). Create minimal dashboard panels.

Day 2 - Alerting and runbook drafts
- Morning: Convert burn-rate thresholds into alert rules, wire to test alert channel.
- Afternoon: Draft runbook containing: detection -> triage -> mitigation steps -> rollback checklist.

Day 3 - Canary + automation pairing
- Morning: Create canary rollout configuration and automated fallback (route X% to smaller model).
- Afternoon: Integrate runbook actions into PagerDuty playbook + demo a simulated incident.

Day 4 - Polish, onboarding template, retro
- Morning: Clean up docs, ensure linked Jira tasks.
- Afternoon: Demo to stakeholders, collect feedback, set follow-ups. Retro + next-steps.

Backlog (micro-projects with owners)
1) inference-api-prod: draft SLO + dashboard panel (Owner: Priya Raman)
   - Tasks: compute error_rate expression, finalize window (30d vs 7d), set target 99.5% for p95 latency <= 300ms; annotate queries with sample traffic pattern notes.
   - Acceptance: PR merged with slo.yml, dashboard panel shows historical compliance.

2) embedder-worker: throughput and queueing SLO (Owner: Mei Chen)
   - Tasks: define queueing latency SLO (95th <= 200ms), create histogram view, add backlog alert when queue > X.
   - Acceptance: Runbook contains mitigation: scale-workers, throttle-client, temp-queue-flush.

3) routing-proxy: regional failover SLO + cost-aware fallback (Owner: Rafael Ortiz)
   - Tasks: define SLO on successful routing within region; add fallback policy when region capacity < 80%.
   - Acceptance: Canary plan implemented and automated traffic-shift script ready in repo.

4) Runbook template + incident playbook (Owner: Ethan Cole)
   - Tasks: produce 2-page runbook template, link to PagerDuty escalation, add postmortem checklist.
   - Acceptance: Template used by at least one pilot service during simulated incident.

5) Observability hygiene: dashboard naming + saved queries (Owner: Anika Patel)
   - Tasks: ensure consistent naming (service.slo.*), tag dashboard panels, create saved PromQL queries.
   - Acceptance: All panels use saved queries and are documented in slo.yml.

Role matrix (who does what during the hackweek)
- SRE (Anika, Ethan): facilitation, SLO design review, runbook vetting, incident simulation.
- Product/Feature PM: define acceptable user-facing windows and business impact, attend demos.
- Serving Runtime (Priya, Rafael): implement canary routing, fallback automation; validate latency signals.
- Platform Observability (Mei): dashboarding, query optimization, test alert plumbing.
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success: provide feature playback scenarios, customer-facing success criteria.

Quick templates (copy-paste)
- Minimal slo.yml:
  name: service-name-slo
  objective: "p95 latency < 300ms"
  target: "99.5%"
  window_days: "30"
  indicators: ["latency_p95_ms", "error_rate"]
  alert_rules: ["burn_rate_high", "error_rate_spike"]

- Runbook skeleton (two pages max):
  1) Summary & SLO statement
  2) How to detect (queries, dashboards)
  3) First response (triage checklist)
  4) Mitigation steps (fast path)
  5) Rollback / fallback (when to flip to smaller model)
  6) Postmortem steps & comms template

Acceptance criteria (team-level)
- SLO file in repo with metadata and linked dashboard ids.
- Dashboard shows historical compliance and is understandable to the product owner.
- Alert rule fires in a test channel and triggers the runbook flow (end-to-end test).
- Canary plan includes automated percentage rollbacks and a manual override.

Open questions / risks
- Data quality: are latency metrics consistent across regions? (ACTION: Priya to validate before Day 1).
- Burn-rate sensitivity: short windows give noisy signals; need decision on default window. Proposed default: 30d rolling with 7d preview.
- Team bandwidth: hackweek may overlap with high-priority incidents—will need exec buy-in to protect time.

Follow-ups (post-hackweek)
- Create SLO onboarding checklist for new services (owner: Anika).
- Align with governance: quarterly SLO review cycle (owner: Platform Eng).
- Roll out a one-click template for canary routing in the serving-runtime repo (owner: Rafael).

Notes to self / rough thoughts
- Keep acceptance light: the goal is operational clarity, not perfect thresholds.
- Prefer 2-page runbooks that engineers will actually read.
- Encourage pairing SRE + product during the measurement debate to avoid back-and-forth.

Fast links / references
- Linear epic SRV-482 (SLO onboarding): https://linear.app/REDWOOD/issue/SRV-482-slo-onboarding
- Observability PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/210
- Slack channel: #ops-chorus (create if missing)

Retrospective prompts (post-event)
- What deliverable provided the most immediate value?
- Which SLOs needed rework after 1 week of live traffic?
- Which automation saved manual steps (and should be prioritized for platform work)?

TODO (short list)
- [ ] Create #ops-chorus Slack channel and invite stakeholders (Anika)
- [ ] Add pilot services metric exports to SRV-482 (Priya)
- [ ] Draft canary traffic-shift script and test in staging (Rafael)
- [ ] Create runbook template PR (Ethan)
- [ ] Schedule kickoff + stakeholder demo times (All)

This doc is intentionally concise and tactical. Use it as the canonical hackweek artifact; move completed artifacts (slo.yml, dashboards, runbooks) into the per-service repo and link back to SRV-482.

End of doc.
